Trina costume.

lines.text:
Who are these little cuties on my head, you ask?
Hehe, they're my family.
Can you hear the sounds of nature?
Trees may seem rough and unrefined, but they actually require a delicate touch.
If you're tired, you're more than free to rest in my embrace for a while.

Ahhh, the pleasant scent of phytoncides...
Oh, is that you, Sun?

Why don't you remove your clothing and get a little closer to nature?
How about joining us, Sun?

Where did you go, Sun?
Does anyone know where Sun might be?

Take your time; there's no rush.
My arms will always be open for you.
Someday, everyone here will feel the beauty of nature, won't they?

It's amazing to see how well they've grown in an artificial environment.
Life always finds a way.
There are so many little ones here who require my care.

They call me Trina, the caretaker of trees.
You're always welcome to rest in my embrace.

I've taken one step closer to nature.
If we shed our layers here, we can take two steps forward.
Wow, the vitality is overflowing.
We must thank Sun, shouldn't we, little ones?

Wow, is this a gift? 
It has been some time since I've received anything like this. I'm touched.
The way you give so generously... you remind me of a tree with abundant fruit.
Thank you. Oh, do you like it as well?
Sun... Is it okay if I hold you close for a moment?
Your body and spirit feel sturdier than any tree I've ever known.

You have this unfailing light that shines on everyone, and I want it all for myself...
Could that be considered greed?
Great. Are we going out for some photosynthesis?
Did you call for me?
I wonder what little ones might be nearby?
It's time to return to nature.
You've set your roots in the wrong place, haven't you?
We need to prune the unnecessary branches.
Careful, so the little ones don't get hurt.
Slow and steady wins the race.
Gently, so the stems don't get damaged.
Hehe, I need to be careful.
Nature is calling to us!
Nature... is a beautiful thing.
Feel the overflowing vitality!
This will make good compost.
Your roots seem to be damaged.
Return to the soil.
That hurts!
Ow!
Oops...
Ugh... This doesn't feel natural...
Hehe, finally, we've borne fruit!
